title: Bistable topological edge states in polariton microcavities with unpaired Dirac cones
authors: Zhuo Zhang, Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Zhen-Nan Tian, Qi-Dai Chen, Yiqi Zhang
abstract: Among the most intriguing properties of honeycomb lattices is the presence of Dirac points that typically emerge in pairs, which can be destroyed by physical effects breaking certain symmetries of the system and leading to nontrivial band topology. We propose a nonlinear microcavity system supporting condensate of exciton-polaritons, where simultaneous breakup of inversion and time-reversal symmetries results in unusual spectrum with unpaired Dirac cones, profoundly affecting the properties of unidirectional edge states. Realized as an array of microcavity pillars, the inversion symmetry is broken by fission of pillar belonging to one of sublattices of honeycomb array into three pillars, while time-reversal symmetry is broken due to interplay of Zeeman splitting in the external magnetic field and spin-orbit coupling. Despite the absence of complete spectral gap, unidirectional edge states may still emerge that can circumvent array corners. Resonant optical pumping leads to reach bistability effects and allow selective excitation of the edge states. We obtain first example of stable localized dissipative edge soliton that circulates along the periphery of insulator over indefinitely long times without radiation. Our results suggest a new platform for nonlinear topological photonics and reveal nontrivial interplay between unpaired Dirac cones and nonlinear effects.
summary: This paper proposes using a modified honeycomb microcavity array to create a platform exhibiting unpaired Dirac cones. By analyzing the nonlinear dynamics under resonant pumping, the authors predict and demonstrate the existence of stable, unidirectional dissipative edge solitons. This work advances topological photonics by showing robust energy localization in an inherently lossy system.
main_problem: The research investigates topological edge states emerging from a nonlinear microcavity system that supports unpaired Dirac cones, an unusual spectral feature.
main_result: The authors demonstrate the existence of stable, unidirectional dissipative edge solitons circulating indefinitely along the periphery of the structure, which is a first example in this context.
method: The study combines linear analysis using Bloch waves and plane-wave expansion with nonlinear time evolution simulations solved via Newton iteration for dissipative states.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as an array of microcavity pillars (fissioned honeycomb structure) supporting exciton-polaritons, governed by coupled Gross-Pitaevskii type equations incorporating spin-orbit coupling and external fields.
key_observables: Unpaired Dirac cones in the band structure, unidirectional edge states bypassing corners, and stable localized dissipative edge solitons.
important_parameters: Spin-orbit coupling strength (beta), polariton loss rate (gamma), and resonant pumping detuning ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific parameter regimes where unpaired Dirac cones appear, and the soliton stability is linked to the presence of fissioned sites.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the linear band structure showing unpaired Dirac cones (Fig. 1), density distributions of bulk vs. edge states (Figs. 4b-d), and time evolution confirming stable circulation of the topological edge soliton (Fig. 6).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the unusual spectral topology (unpaired Dirac cones) in the linear regime, to analyzing the emergence of topologically protected edge states, and finally investigating the nonlinear dynamics leading to bistability and persistent dissipative solitons.
why_interesting: This work bridges topological physics with nonlinear optics/photonics by demonstrating robust, non-dissipative-like behavior (solitons) in a fundamentally dissipative quantum system, which is highly relevant for engineered light-matter interactions.
